newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LG Semicon sees H1 net sharply falling.
newsitem.headline: LG Semicon sees H1 net sharply falling.

text.p: South Korean chipmaker LG Semicon Co forecast after-tax net profit for the first half of calendar 1997 to plunge to around 30 billion won from a 132.7 billion won profit a year earlier, a company official said on Wednesday.
The official, who declined to be identified, said the company's six months sales were estimated at 850 billion won, also down sharply from 1.19 trillion won in the same 1996 period.
LG Semicon, an affiliate of the LG Group, is due to release its final half-year results on August 15.
"The plunges in sales and profits were because of sharp drops in memory chip prices from a year earlier," the official told Reuters.

The unit price for 16-megabyte dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, the current mainstay of computer memory chips, had fallen to $6-$10 during the first half from an average of around $30 a year earlier, the official said.
The company, however, expected a rising demand for 64-megabyte chips to help boost the bottom line for its yearly profits.
The company is one of South Korea's top three DRAM makers.
LG Semicon targeted a net profit of 120 billion won for the whole of this year, comparing with a 91.1 billion won profit last year, the official said.
The company also projected sales of 2.4 trillion won for this year, up from 2.01 trillion won posted in calendar 1996.
